subject: lavaGolem
pitch:
Category: Monster.
Subject: lava golem of basalt plates and molten seams.
Style: Genshin Impact.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but quality lava golem model, about 2.6m tall, with a humanoid skeleton including hips, spine, neck, head, jaw, and articulated arms and legs in a T-ish rest pose.

Working out the toon kit imports for a Genshin-style basalt look with glowing orange cel shading, then calculating limb lengths, joint positions, and chain definitions for the legs and spine so the proportions stay anatomically plausible without being able to test it directly.

Now I'm structuring the torso as a lofted mesh bound to the spine chain, adding a pelvis box, and setting up the neck and head joints so the chain connects cleanly from the hips through the spine to the head.

Still placing body parts...

I'll keep the basalt paint with bright orange crack cells and layer glowing elements separately—chest core, eyes, mouth, seam strips, knuckle cracks, fingertips, shoulder magma—using toon-style cel shading so the cracks still shade correctly under lighting. For the fists, I'm building each as a big box with three finger boxes attached to the wrist bone, pulling tip joints from the chain.

For fingers I'll keep it simple with short two-point chains per digit, parented to the wrist tip and swept outward and slightly down, rather than building full articulated joints. Then I'll add armor plates—shoulder pauldrons, chest plates, spine spikes, knee plates, foot blocks—plus a glowing octahedral magma core in the chest with a rune texture, skipping the floating belt idea for now.

Now I'm adding glowing seam strips on the chest using rod connectors in a zigzag, scattering about 14 basalt shard cones across the back of the torso surface, and designing a slit-eyed orange glow texture with mirrored left/right SVGs before setting up the box-shaped foot parts at the ankle joint.

Working out the leg geometry now — knee sphere plates, tapering leg tubes, and torso loft stations with varying widths and heights going up the body.

I'm also figuring out head placement relative to torso top, plus the spine chain points and where to anchor a chest core glow element relative to torso depth.

Now I'm working through the chest core glow detail—placing an octahedron with a ring of small spikes or cones around it, then adding rod-like glowing seams radiating outward from the core across the torso surface, trying to snap them to the curved surface so they don't float or sink into the mesh.

Next I'm tackling the facial structure: positioning the head and jaw boxes with their own bone, a jaw joint for articulation, and planning a glowing rectangle for the mouth set into the lower front of the head.
